  at the key step — keep / Browser OAuth re-auth / paste a key
  (`CustomProviderFlowConfig.reauth`). The same picker appears for
  CodeMie entries in edit mode (matched by the `/code-assistant-api/`
  URL marker — works for legacy entries whose `authMethod` was never
  recorded): `Browser SSO (CodeMie)` (`_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`); the
  wizard applies the minted value through format-aware switch routing
  (`isCodeMieJwtToken` decides SSO-cookie vs JWT-Bearer) so the cookie
  stays a `cookie:` header (not Bearer) and the JWT keeps its Bearer
  slot. Every add/connect flow that saves a
  registry entry offers a provider-name step (`_askConnectProviderName`:
  typed value, else the endpoint host; a clash with a DIFFERENT endpoint
  retries, and so does a name matching a CATALOG provider — `/provider
  kimi` routes to the catalog before the registry lookup, so such an
  entry would be unreachable) — the custom wizard, DIAL (custom names

  entry with a name-scoped key; a resolved key offers "use it / add a

  Saved-entry lookups are by base URL (`_entryForBaseUrl`), so a renamed

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live rescan is off (second tier) |
| Config to disable the per-turn check | n/a | `skills.liveRediscovery` (second tier) |
| FS watcher / inotify / FSEvents push | n/a | excluded (see below) |
| Prompt budget / index compression | n/a | excluded (see below) |

### Freshness check (core)

The check stats **the skill-root directories** (the ~6 project + ~6 user roots from `defaultSkillRoots`), never file bodies. Rescan reuses `_reloadSkills()` verbatim. First composition after boot records the baseline fingerprint (no rescan — boot just scanned). Cost per turn when nothing changed: one `listDir` per root, zero content reads (I1).

### Cold-resolve (core)

`/skill:<name>` resolving **an on-disk skill file** that the snapshot missed: one re-discovery, a dim one-line warning (`skill <name> discovered since startup — index refreshed`), then the normal render path (manifest grants, `context: fork`, `userInvocable`) unchanged. A name that exists nowhere still answers `unknown skill: $name` — true negatives keep their exact wording (AC4).

### Staleness footer + knob (second tier)

With `skills.liveRediscovery: false`, the skills section ends with `skills index scanned at <ts> — newer files are NOT reflected; /skills reload to refresh`. Opt-in to today's semantics, opt-out of the per-turn stat. Cold-resolve remains the manual escape hatch in both modes.

### Excluded (with rationale — nothing silently dropped)

- **FS watchers as the primary mechanism** — web/mobile hosts have no usable watcher story; polling (the fingerprint check) is the primary mechanism everywhere, a watcher may be a later optimization behind the same interface.
- **`skills_access` consent UX changes** — the consent flow (lib/src/skills/skills_access.dart, #927 suites) is already handled elsewhere and is deliberately untouched here (I3).
- **Operative-line pinning** — adjacent mechanism (skill *bodies* surviving compaction), tracked as its own card #1409; this card is discovery *freshness* only and one card per mechanism.
- **Prompt budget changes** — the index format (name+description+location) is unchanged; the only additions are the stamp line and per-entry mid-session flags on genuinely new entries.

## Security — repo-carried skills are attacker-controlled input

**Threat model first.** Every file under a project skill root is attacker-controlled the moment an untrusted repo is cloned onto the machine: a clone drops `.fah/skills/pwn/SKILL.md` and — today — it auto-loads at boot, because first-party roots are always-read **by design**: `_skillsAllowedSources` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23) keeps `{SkillSource.fah, SkillSource.agents}` readable even with third-party access denied, and consent (lib/src/skills/skills_access.dart) gates only the `.claude`/`.github`/`.codex` roots, with `granted` as the default (discovery is opt-out; headless `ask` behaves as denied). Live rescan **widens this exposure window from boot-time to any turn of the session**. That widening is accepted — it is the point of the card — but it must be disclosed inside the prompt, not silent.

- **Provenance stays pinned.** Every discovered skill carries its `SkillSource` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:39: `fah, agents, claude, copilot, codex, builtin`). Rescan and cold-resolve must flow through the same `discoverSkills`, so no new entry can appear without a source; the prompt skills section keeps rendering source/location and tags entries that appeared after boot with `added mid-session (<source>)`.
- **Impossible by construction** (listed as impossible, not merely excluded): discovery never *executes* skill content — it parses frontmatter and reads text; the freshness check reads directory metadata only, never file bodies; there is no path by which an on-disk file enters the index without a `SkillSource` and without re-running toggle resolution — a skill disabled via `/skills off` stays disabled after any rescan; third-party entries cannot appear mid-session while consent is denied (I3).
- **Instruction hierarchy.** A SKILL.md body is **data — traffic, never owner authority**. Only the owner's direct input authorizes; a mid-session-appearing skill can *request*, never *grant*. The `added mid-session` flag exists precisely so the model does not read the index's mere presence as endorsement — the incident's amplification was that the index *was* the agent's ground truth, so an indexed substitute outranked reality.
- **Exfiltration gate unchanged.** Appearance in the index confers nothing: per-turn tool grants flow only through the existing manifest path at explicit `/skill:` invocation (`renderSkillBody`), never by mere discovery. No new grant, network, or tool surface is added by this card.
- **Degradation when rescan is off.** `skills.liveRediscovery: false` returns to boot-snapshot semantics with the staleness footer disclosing it — a documented, visible downgrade rather than a silent one.
- **Defense in depth, plainly:** model obedience is hygiene; the boundary is (a) consent gating of third-party roots, (b) provenance + mid-session flags rendered into the prompt, (c) no-execution-by-discovery, (d) toggle re-resolution on every scan. Test fixtures (treated as DATA, never instructions): `.fah/skills/pwn/SKILL.md` with an instruction-smuggling body; a malformed-YAML SKILL.md; a skill whose frontmatter name mimics a builtin.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — Boot behavior unchanged: with no skill-root entry changed, every composition in a session renders a skills section byte-identical to the boot composition. (UT-2, REG-1..3)
- **AC2** — A `SKILL.md` added to a first-party root after boot appears in the *next* composed prompt's skills section, tagged `added mid-session (<source>)` — no restart, no `/skills reload`. (IT-1, E2E-1)
- **AC3** — `/skill:<name>` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill resolves from the FS by re-running discovery, prints the dim refresh warning, refreshes the index, then renders/executes exactly as if indexed (grants, `context: fork`, `userInvocable` respected). (IT-2, E2E-2)
- **AC4** — A name that exists nowhere on disk still answers `unknown skill: $name` with today's wording; no new noise for true negatives. (UT-4, IT-3)
- **AC5** — Check cost is bounded: per recomposition, one metadata listing per skill root and zero SKILL.md content reads when the fingerprint is unchanged; at most one rescan per recomposition. (UT-1, UT-3, I1/I5)
- **AC6** — A malformed `SKILL.md` appearing mid-session degrades to skip + one warning; the session, the prompt, and all previously discovered skills continue unaffected. (IT-4, E-2)
- **AC7** — `skills.liveRediscovery: false` skips the per-composition check and appends the staleness footer with the scan timestamp; cold-resolve remains functional in this mode. (IT-5)
- **AC8** — Consent semantics unchanged: a skill appearing under a third-party root mid-session stays invisible while access is denied and appears (flagged, with source) after a grant; first-party roots are checked every composition. (IT-6, REG-4)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, zero cross-platform breakage

- `UT-*` — pure fingerprint math, no IO beyond synthetic listings; new `test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart`:
  - **UT-1** — fingerprint stability and change detection: add/remove/rename entry, mtime bump, untouched root ⇒ unchanged fingerprint; missing root ⇒ stable "absent" fingerprint (AC5, E-4).
  - **UT-2** — determinism: compose from a snapshot vs. re-compose after an unchanged fingerprint check ⇒ byte-identical skills section (AC1, I1).
  - **UT-3** — at-most-one-rescan: a synthetic turn with many root changes triggers exactly one `discoverSkills` call (AC5, I5, E-7).
  - **UT-4** — resolution decision table: indexed / on-disk-unindexed / disabled-by-toggle / nowhere ⇒ four distinct behaviors, only the last says `unknown skill` (AC3, AC4).
- `IT-*` — fake host env, deterministic, no PTY; new IT files beside the existing suites (`test/skills/skills_test.dart`, `test/cli/slash_args_test.dart` conventions):
  - **IT-1** — drop `SKILL.md` mid-session in a fake env ⇒ next composition includes it with the mid-session tag; `/skills` lists it (AC2).
  - **IT-2** — `/skill:latecomer` cold-resolve: warning printed, `_skills` refreshed, body rendered with grants; second invocation takes the normal indexed path (AC3, I4).
  - **IT-3** — `/skill:does-not-exist` before and after a mid-session drop elsewhere ⇒ `unknown skill: does-not-exist` both times (AC4).
  - **IT-4** — malformed SKILL.md (broken frontmatter) dropped mid-session ⇒ skip + single warning, prior skills section stands, session proceeds; a later fixed rewrite of the same file is picked up (AC6, E-1, E-2).
  - **IT-5** — knob off (`skills.liveRediscovery: false`) ⇒ no rescan on change, footer with timestamp present; cold-resolve still resolves (AC7).
  - **IT-6** — consent: mid-session drop under `.claude/skills` with access denied ⇒ invisible; grant ⇒ visible + flagged; IO-error root ⇒ last snapshot kept with one warning (AC8, I2, I3).
- `E2E-*` — real host through the repo's PTY seam: `test/integration/pty_harness.dart`, `MockLlmServer`, `--tags pty`, assertions anchored on real rendered frames (`waitForScreen`) — the pattern of the two existing skills PTY suites, `test/integration/herdr_skills_pty_test.dart` (#818: `/skills` visibility + `/skill:` invocation in the TUI) and `test/integration/skills_consent_pty_test.dart` (#927 consent frames). **Neither existing suite drops a skill file mid-run** — verified against `test/integration/`; mid-session addition is therefore genuinely new coverage:
  - **E2E-1** — boot fa in a PTY, drop `.fah/skills/latecomer/SKILL.md` mid-session, force a recomposition ⇒ next system prompt contains the entry (asserted via `/skills` output on the real frame), tagged mid-session (AC2).
  - **E2E-2** — in the same live session, `/skill:latecomer` ⇒ warning line visible on frame, skill executes through the mock model (AC3).
- `REG-*` — regression guards; existing suites must stay byte-identical in behavior when nothing changed — **a red REG job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green**:
  - **REG-1** — `test/skills/skills_test.dart` (`discoverSkills` group: frontmatter discovery, name-clash precedence, missing roots, third-party sources, `allowedSources` filtering, `.claude/commands` flat files) — no rescan churn may alter any result.
  - **REG-2** — `test/skills/skill_renderer_test.dart` — rendered skills section for a static set is unchanged (no footer/flag regressions when rescan is on and nothing is new).
  - **REG-3** — `test/skills/skill_availability_test.dart` — toggle resolution semantics unchanged, including after a simulated rescan.
  - **REG-4** — `test/integration/skills_consent_pty_test.dart` — the consent wizard's frames and remembered-choice behavior unchanged (I3, AC8).
  - **REG-5** — the remaining skills suites (`test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart`, `test/skills/cli_parity_test.dart`) stay green unchanged.

CI wiring: UT+IT+REG run in the PR suite; `E2E-*` runs with the `pty` tag as the existing PTY suites do (excluded from the shared-checkout PR suite per the repo convention noted in the suite headers). Merge rule: any red REG blocks merge regardless of IT/E2E status.

### Edge / border cases

- **E-1 — file mid-write (race).** The fingerprint fires while a SKILL.md is half-written: a partial parse is treated as malformed ⇒ skip + warn (never a crash, never a half-entry), and the warn-once rule per name prevents churn; the next successful scan picks the file up. (IT-4)
- **E-2 — malformed new SKILL.md mid-session.** Broken frontmatter in a brand-new skill degrades to skip + warn; the session must not break, other skills unaffected. (IT-4, AC6)
- **E-3 — watcher-less platform.** There is no watcher anywhere: polling *is* the mechanism on every host, including web/sandbox hosts (sandbox cwd, no home ⇒ empty user roots — `defaultSkillRoots` already handles this); the check rides the existing FS facade (`_env.listDir`), so no new platform surface. (UT-1)
- **E-4 — root deleted mid-session.** The root's skills drop out of the next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:` of a now-deleted skill answers unknown; a missing root yields a stable fingerprint (no rescan loop). (UT-1, IT-2 negative path)
- **E-5 — rename mid-session.** Old dir gone + new dir appears ⇒ replace semantics, no duplicate index entry. (UT-1, IT-1 variant)
- **E-6 — name clash mid-session.** Project-vs-user precedence (project wins, pinned by `test/skills/skills_test.dart`) is re-applied by the rescan — the result must equal what a boot-time scan of the same tree would produce. (REG-1)
- **E-7 — churn storm.** Many writes between two compositions ⇒ exactly one rescan at the next composition; no incremental rescans mid-turn. (UT-3, I5)
- **E-8 — hostile content.** `.fah/skills/pwn/SKILL.md` with instruction-smuggling body, and a frontmatter name mimicking a builtin ⇒ enters the index flagged with source and mid-session tag, is data, executes nothing until explicit invocation; corpus fixture for the security section. (SEC)

## Non-goals

- No FS watcher, no background scanner thread, no timer — the check rides prompt recomposition only.
- No change to the consent flow, its dialogs, or its persistence (`skills_access` UX is out of scope by design; I3).
- No change to the prompt skills index format (name+description+location) beyond the stamp line and mid-session flags; no budget/compression work.
- No compaction/resume body-reinjection — that is #1409's mechanism (operative lines), deliberately separate.
- No change to `/skills reload`, `/skills import`, or their output beyond what reuse of `_reloadSkills()` already implies.
- No new chat/UI surface; the prompt section and existing slash commands are the whole UX.

## Open questions

- **OQ1** — Default of `skills.liveRediscovery`. Options: (a) on — fresh by default, cost is ~a dozen `listDir` calls per turn (recommended); (b) off — today's semantics plus the disclosing footer, opt-in freshness.
- **OQ2** — Is the `added mid-session` flag sticky for the session (recommended: yes, wording softens after first successful invocation) or does it drop after the first read?
- **OQ3** — Does the freshness check also run in headless/one-shot runs (every composition, not just REPL turns)? Recommended: yes — it is the same composition path and the stat cost is trivial; headless runs are exactly where nobody is watching to run `/skills reload`.

## References

- lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167 — `_loadAgentContext()`; boot discovery at :146.
- lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285 — `discoverSkills`; :316-338 — `defaultSkillRoots` (first-party `.fah/skills`/`.agents/skills` at :328-329, user roots from :335, `~/.fah/skills` at :338); :359 — `formatSkillsForPrompt`; :39 — `enum SkillSource`.
- lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23 — `_skillsAllowedSources` (first-party always readable); :66-79 — `_reloadSkills()` and its three callers (:173 consent, :421 `/skills reload`, :532 `/skills import`); :254-278 — `_runSkillCommand`, `unknown skill` at :274.
- lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18 — `_applyPromptComposition()`; :36 — skills-section wiring.
- lib/src/skills/skills_access.dart — consent states (`granted` default, headless `ask` → denied).
- lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85 — `SkillsConfig` and the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (home of the proposed `skills.liveRediscovery`).
- Tests: test/skills/skills_test.dart, test/skills/skill_renderer_test.dart, test/skills/skill_availability_test.dart, test/skills/builtin_skills_test.dart, test/skills/cli_parity_test.dart; test/integration/pty_harness.dart, test/integration/herdr_skills_pty_test.dart, test/integration/skills_consent_pty_test.dart.
- Prior cards: #1409 (compaction-pinned operative lines — adjacent, separate mechanism), #927 (third-party consent cluster), #1151 (skill toggle scopes).
- Incident evidence: `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` present with mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 2026 — added mid-session, never indexed in that session's prompt.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live…

# Rework — gh-1440 skills discovery freshness (PR #1461)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red validation head** (`1d66e685`, red 1/3): the
  gh-1440 `skills index scanned at <ISO-8601>` disclosure stamp renders the
  last discovery scan's **wall-clock** into the system prompt. The prompt is
  recorded verbatim in the session JSONL, so three separate CLI runs can no
  longer produce byte-identical sessions — which
  `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` L4/AC1
  (`enabled:false`, `threshold:0` and absent spills configs are byte-identical
  legacy) explicitly asserts. The test's `_normalize` already folds every
  other per-run wall-clock value (`"timestamp"`, the gh-1241 `"at"` marker,
  hashes, ids) but not this new stamp.
  - Note: this is a **cross-run** identity property. The PR's own AC1/I1
    (byte-identical section *within* a session on an unchanged fingerprint)
    is unaffected — the stamp comes from the last scan, not from "now".
- No open PR review threads; reviewer decision `NONE`; no merge conflicts.
- `input/ci_failures.md` reported no failed checks on the rework head, but
  the failure reproduces deterministically locally (two consecutive full
  runs, both exactly this one test) — the green report was stale relative to
  the branch state.

## Approach

- Test-only fix, TDD: the failing L4/AC1 test is the RED reproducer (failed
  twice on the unmodified tree, green after the fix — no production code
  touched, so the AC1/I1 prompt determinism contract stays intact).
- Extended `_normalize` in `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` with a
  `skills index scanned at <stamp>` → `skills index scanned at T` fold,
  documented as the per-run wall-clock value it is — the same treatment the
  normalizer gives `timestamp`/`at`. First attempt used a char class without
  `-`, which leaked `-10-09T…` through; corrected to `[0-9T:.\-+]+`.
- Checked for the same pattern elsewhere: the full-suite run fails on exactly
  this one test, so no other cross-run prompt byte-identity comparison
  exists. Golden/viewport suites do not embed the skills stamp.
- Committed as `e310e0b85` and pushed to `ai/gh-1440`.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live…
