# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 17 - **Additions**: +1442 - **Deletions**: -28 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:31:28Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live…

# Rework — gh-1440 skills discovery freshness (PR #1461)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red validation head** (`1d66e685`, red 1/3): the

  last discovery scan's **wall-clock** into the system prompt. The prompt is
  recorded verbatim in the session JSONL, so three separate CLI runs can no
  longer produce byte-identical sessions — which
  `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` L4/AC1
  (`enabled:false`, `threshold:0` and absent spills configs are byte-identical
  legacy) explicitly asserts. The test's `_normalize` already folds every
  other per-run wall-clock value (`"timestamp"`, the gh-1241 `"at"` marker,
  hashes, ids) but not this new stamp.

    (byte-identical section *within* a session on an unchanged fingerprint)
    is unaffected — the stamp comes from the last scan, not from "now".
- No open PR review threads; reviewer decision `NONE`; no merge conflicts.

  the failure reproduces deterministically locally (two consecutive full
  runs, both exactly this one test) — the green report was stale relative to

  `skills index scanned at <stamp>` → `skills index scanned at T` fold,
  documented as the per-run wall-clock value it is — the same treatment the
  normalizer gives `timestamp`/`at`. First attempt used a char class without
  `-`, which leaked `-10-09T…` through; corrected to `[0-9T:.\-+]+`.

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.

      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on

      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 17 - **Additions**: +1442 - **Deletions**: -28 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T00:31:28Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

          python-version: '3.x'

      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live…

# Rework — gh-1440 skills discovery freshness (PR #1461)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red validation head** (`1d66e685`, red 1/3): the
  gh-1440 `skills index scanned at <ISO-8601>` disclosure stamp renders the
  last discovery scan's **wall-clock** into the system prompt. The prompt is
  recorded verbatim in the session JSONL, so three separate CLI runs can no
  longer produce byte-identical sessions — which
  `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` L4/AC1
  (`enabled:false`, `threshold:0` and absent spills configs are byte-identical
  legacy) explicitly asserts. The test's `_normalize` already folds every
  other per-run wall-clock value (`"timestamp"`, the gh-1241 `"at"` marker,
  hashes, ids) but not this new stamp.
  - Note: this is a **cross-run** identity property. The PR's own AC1/I1
    (byte-identical section *within* a session on an unchanged fingerprint)
    is unaffected — the stamp comes from the last scan, not from "now".
- No open PR review threads; reviewer decision `NONE`; no merge conflicts.
- `input/ci_failures.md` reported no failed checks on the rework head, but
  the failure reproduces deterministically locally (two consecutive full
  runs, both exactly this one test) — the green report was stale relative to
  the branch state.

## Approach

- Test-only fix, TDD: the failing L4/AC1 test is the RED reproducer (failed
  twice on the unmodified tree, green after the fix — no production code
  touched, so the AC1/I1 prompt determinism contract stays intact).
- Extended `_normalize` in `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` with a
  `skills index scanned at <stamp>` → `skills index scanned at T` fold,
  documented as the per-run wall-clock value it is — the same treatment the
  normalizer gives `timestamp`/`at`. First attempt used a char class without
  `-`, which leaked `-10-09T…` through; corrected to `[0-9T:.\-+]+`.
- Checked for the same pattern elsewhere: the full-suite run fails on exactly
  this one test, so no other cross-run prompt byte-identity comparison
  exists. Golden/viewport suites do not embed the skills stamp.
- Committed as `e310e0b85` and pushed to `ai/gh-1440`.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` — `_normalize` folds the

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline

      # Issue #1234 rework: 0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override (a
      # gates.loc.sources key is a ConfigException — caught here on
      # 019ede65), and the package config's sources drive the CRAP census
      # too, so test/ + example/ get the SAME loc gate from the companion
      # config (crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml) — the scope the retired shell
      # guards (gh-1232) scanned there. No baseline: nothing exceeds 2800
      # today, and the ceiling itself is the point.
      - name: Loc scope gate (test/ + example/, gh-1232 whole-tree ceiling)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo: 12.0 (re-measured whole-tree on
  # the merged-suite lcov, #1234 rework). The card's named offenders DID
  # move — readPasteboardImage 16.32 (split into fake-seam /
  # platform-dispatch helpers), the CC-12 trio (_handleTreeKey,
  # discoverTaskAgents, _rebuild) split into cohesive sub-dispatchers,
  # the four 0%-cov CC-3 methods covered by tests (frontmatter, video
  # endpoint, below-window ingest, provider picker), the named CC-9 tier
  # split, and _listModels (20 @ 0%) covered by the line-mode /models
  # test. But the FIRST real whole-tree measurement (the authoring box
  # had no dart toolchain) shows the 12.0 → 8.0 repin is not earned yet:
  # 137 methods measure above 8.0 — 54 at exactly 12.00 (the CC-3 @ 0%
  # tier + fully-covered CC-12 dispatchers) and 83 at 9.00 (CC-9 @ 100%).
  # Threshold stays at the measured max; the 12.00/9.00 tier is the next
  # ladder card (cover the CC-3@0% half, split the CC-12 dispatchers,
  # then the threshold follows down to 8.0). Only down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
  # _listModels used to hit 20 with 0% coverage (line-mode-only output);
  # covered by test/cli/provider_models_line_mode_test.dart in #1234.

# ─── loc gate (issue #1234, gh-1232 migration) ─────────────────────────────
# The ≤2800-line file guard MOVED from scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh stage_size +
# the ci.yml shell find-exec guards onto crap4dart's `loc` gate (0.11.0,
# maintainer-confirmed wc -l semantics). Enforced whole-tree on every merge
# validation via `crap4dart check --baseline` (CI quality-gates step) and
# staged files in the pre-commit hook — no staged-scoping escape, no
# hook-dependence, merge-bot merges included. max_lines only DOWN;
# app_localizations.dart is gen-l10n OUTPUT (no .g.dart suffix) — excluded,
# not baselined.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# gh-1440: [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth)

## Description

## Goal — Skills discovery freshness (v1, initial)

One sentence: **A skill that lands on disk mid-session becomes visible in the very next prompt composition and `/skill:` invocation — the discovered-skills index becomes a cache with a declared freshness contract, instead of a boot-time snapshot the agent reads as exhaustive ground truth for "what skills exist".**

Today, skills are discovered exactly once per process: `_loadAgentContext()` runs `_skills = await discoverSkills(...)` at boot (lib/src/cli/agent_cli_lifecycle.dart:143-167, the assignment at :146; roots from `defaultSkillRoots`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the system prompt's skills section is rendered from that snapshot (`formatSkillsForPrompt`, lib/src/skills/skills.dart:359, wired at lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:36). The only refresh path is `_reloadSkills()` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:66-79) and it has exactly three callers: the consent change `_setSkillsAccess` (:173), `/skills reload` (:421), and `/skills import` (:532). There is no mtime check, no per-turn rescan, and no filesystem fallback in `/skill:<name>` (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278 — resolution consults only the in-memory `_enabledSkills`/`_skills` lists and answers `unknown skill: $name` at :274). This card adds a cheap freshness check at every prompt recomposition plus a cold-resolve path for `/skill:<name>`.

## Why this framing (the incident, and the framings it kills)

Real incident, 2026-10-08. The owner ordered the chief agent to use the project skill `fa-self-improve`. That skill had been added to `.fah/skills/fa-self-improve/SKILL.md` mid-session by another agent (mtime Oct 8 15:43:13 — verified on disk the entire time). Because the chief's system-prompt available-skills index is a boot snapshot, the skill was not in it, and the chief (a) told the owner no such skill exists, then (b) substituted the closest *indexed* skill (`create-goal`) and filed a card violating `fa-self-improve`'s own protocol. Cost: owner trust plus wasted turns. The substitution looked legitimate precisely because the substitute was indexed — the index read as exhaustive truth, so "not in the index" collapsed into "does not exist".

Root mechanics, each load-bearing and verifiable in the working tree:

- **(a) One-shot discovery.** `_loadAgentContext()` snapshots skills once at boot; nothing re-runs `discoverSkills` for the life of the process except the three `_reloadSkills()` callers above. No mtime check, no per-turn rescan (no `stat`/mtime logic anywhere in lib/src/skills/skills.dart).
- **(b) The index is the only surface the agent consults.** The prompt's skills section (name+description+location, `formatSkillsForPrompt`) is read by the agent as exhaustive ground truth for existence claims. There is no FS existence check at invocation time either: `_runSkillCommand` answers `unknown skill` from the same snapshot.
- **(c) Self-precedent amplifies.** A wrong-but-indexed substitute (here: `create-goal`) looks legitimate because the agent's own context endorses it. An unindexed skill cannot even lose to it — it is invisible.

Retracted framings (considered and dropped, so no owner re-litigates them):

- **"The index is wrong"** — retracted: the index is correct *as of its scan*. The correct frame is cache/freshness: a cache without a freshness contract that consumers treat as truth.
- **"Rescan unconditionally every turn"** — retracted: wasteful and pointless when nothing changed; the check must be stat-cheap and rescan only on detected change (invariant I1).
- **"Tell the model to re-check the filesystem when a skill seems missing"** — retracted: prompt discipline without a mechanical carrier is exactly the failure class of this incident. The carrier here is the rescan + cold-resolve, not a plea.

## Architecture

Named components, all derived state — the session JSONL stays byte-identical, and no new process or watcher is introduced:

```
skill roots (.fah/skills, .agents/skills, 3rd-party, user roots)
        │  cheap stat: one directory listing per root, no content reads
        ▼
SkillRootsFingerprint ── unchanged ──▶ compose prompt from _skills (byte-identical, zero reads)
        │ changed (or first composition after boot)
        ▼
discoverSkills (same roots, same consent gate) ──▶ _skills refreshed
        │                                            │
        ▼                                            ▼
_applyPromptComposition()                    prompt skills section stamps
(lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18)       "scanned at <ts>" + per-entry
                                             "added mid-session" flags
/skill:<name> miss ──▶ coldSkillResolve(): re-run discoverSkills;
                       hit → warn "discovered since startup — index refreshed",
                       reload, render as normal; true miss → unknown skill
```

- **`SkillRootsFingerprint`** — a stat-level stamp of the handful of skill-root directories (entry names + mtimes; missing root = stable "absent" fingerprint). Computed inside the recomposition path (`_applyPromptComposition`, lib/src/cli/agent_cli_prompt.dart:18) before rendering the skills section.
- **Freshness check** — compares the fingerprint to the last scan's; on change, re-runs the existing `discoverSkills` (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:285) with the same roots (lib/src/skills/skills.dart:316-338) and the same consent gate (`_skillsAllowedSources`, lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:20-23), then `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + recompose — the exact body of `_reloadSkills()`, reused, not duplicated.
- **`coldSkillResolve()`** — the `/skill:<name>` miss path (lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:254-278): before answering `unknown skill`, re-run discovery once; a hit prints a one-line warning, refreshes the index, and renders as if indexed. Respect `userInvocable` and toggles exactly as the indexed path does.
- **`skills.liveRediscovery`** — a new `skills:` section key, sibling of the reserved `access`/`disableShellExecution` keys (parser: `SkillsConfig`/CLI config, lib/src/skills/skill_availability.dart:50-85). When off, the per-composition check is skipped and the prompt skills section carries a staleness footer; cold-resolve stays available regardless (manual override).

Invariants, each asserted by a test:

- **I1** — unchanged fingerprint ⇒ zero skill-content reads and a skills section byte-identical to the previous composition (prompt determinism; UT-2, REG-1..3).
- **I2** — any freshness-check failure (IO error, unreadable root) keeps the last good snapshot, warns once, and never blocks composition or the turn (IT-6).
- **I3** — first-party roots are always stat'ed; third-party roots are stat'ed/read only under granted consent. Consent semantics are untouched (IT-5, REG-4).
- **I4** — cold-resolve re-runs full `discoverSkills` (provenance, manifest parse, toggle resolution) — there is no ad-hoc file-read side door (IT-2, SEC).
- **I5** — at most one rescan per recomposition; no loops, no watcher (UT-3, E-7).

## Capability surface (what the filesystem allows → our shape)

| FS event during a session | Today | This card |
|---|---|---|
| New skill dir under a first-party root | invisible until restart / `/skills reload` / import / consent change | visible in next composition, flagged `added mid-session` (core) |
| Skill file edited mid-session | stale body+description served | body re-read at invocation as today; index entry refreshed on fingerprint change (core) |
| Skill dir removed mid-session | stays indexed forever | dropped from next composition with a one-line note; `/skill:name` → unknown (core) |
| `/skill:<name>` of unindexed-but-on-disk skill | `unknown skill: $name` (:274) | cold-resolve from FS with warning + index refresh (core) |
| New skill under a third-party root | invisible (consent) | invisible until consent; appears flagged after grant — consent UX unchanged (core, I3) |
| Prompt discloses index freshness | never | stamp `scanned at <ts>` always; explicit staleness footer when live…

# Rework — gh-1440 skills discovery freshness (PR #1461)

## Issues/Notes

- **Root cause of the red validation head** (`1d66e685`, red 1/3): the
  gh-1440 `skills index scanned at <ISO-8601>` disclosure stamp renders the
  last discovery scan's **wall-clock** into the system prompt. The prompt is
  recorded verbatim in the session JSONL, so three separate CLI runs can no
  longer produce byte-identical sessions — which
  `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` L4/AC1
  (`enabled:false`, `threshold:0` and absent spills configs are byte-identical
  legacy) explicitly asserts. The test's `_normalize` already folds every
  other per-run wall-clock value (`"timestamp"`, the gh-1241 `"at"` marker,
  hashes, ids) but not this new stamp.
  - Note: this is a **cross-run** identity property. The PR's own AC1/I1
    (byte-identical section *within* a session on an unchanged fingerprint)
    is unaffected — the stamp comes from the last scan, not from "now".
- No open PR review threads; reviewer decision `NONE`; no merge conflicts.

  the failure reproduces deterministically locally (two consecutive full
  runs, both exactly this one test) — the green report was stale relative to
  the branch state.

- Test-only fix, TDD: the failing L4/AC1 test is the RED reproducer (failed
  twice on the unmodified tree, green after the fix — no production code
  touched, so the AC1/I1 prompt determinism contract stays intact).
- Extended `_normalize` in `test/cli/agent_cli_spilling_test.dart` with a
  `skills index scanned at <stamp>` → `skills index scanned at T` fold,
  documented as the per-run wall-clock value it is — the same treatment the
  normalizer gives `timestamp`/`at`. First attempt used a char class without
  `-`, which leaked `-10-09T…` through; corrected to `[0-9T:.\-+]+`.

name: CRAP + duplication
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [changes, test-core]
    timeout-minutes: 6
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Scope fastpass (out-of-scope → green in seconds)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.shared != 'true' && needs.changes.outputs.app != 'true'
        run: echo "no core/shared/app changes — guards green-skipped (required context reported)"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.app == 'true'

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Pub cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: pub-${{ runner.os }}-

      # Same scope gate as every other step here: on a skipped (app-only)
      # PR no dart SDK is set up, so an unconditional pub get dies with 127.
      - run: dart pub get
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: coverage-shard-*
          path: coverage-shards

      - name: Merge shard coverage (union DA hits per file, NOT cat)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          mkdir -p coverage
          python3 scripts/merge_lcov.py -o coverage/lcov.info coverage-shards/*/lcov.info

      - name: CRAP ratchet (threshold pinned in crap4dart.yaml)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          # Issue #447: 0.9.5+ carries the gate framework (broken_goldens
          # et al.); 0.2.1 knew only the CRAP ratchet. Both configs set
          # coverage.run_tests: false — the merged shard lcov above is the
          # coverage source; gates must not re-run the suite.
          # gh-1061: >=0.10.0 — analyzer 7.3→14.4 refresh + the
          # duplication.sources key (native cross-module scan).
          # gh-1106: >=0.11.0 — Type-2 renamed-clone detection
          # (duplication.ignore_locals) + gate baselines; the
          # duplication gate config throws on older parsers (unknown
          # keys are a ConfigException).
          # Bounded (rework review): a floating >= would auto-adopt
          # 0.12.0+ with no repo change — bump the ceiling deliberately.
          dart pub global activate crap4dart ">=0.11.0 <0.12.0"
          dart pub global run crap4dart analyze

      - name: Quality gates (broken goldens + Type-2 duplication, issue 1106)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline
