Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }

skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'

}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown

---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in

  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac

  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;

  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac

  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then

    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. `loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

body

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then

fi

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;

  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"
  ARGS=(api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}"
    -f branch="${DATA_BRANCH}"
    -f message="leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]"
    -f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)")

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;

This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve block added ~4 branches); at 75.6% merged coverage that measures CRAP 15.45 against the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CRAP ratchet failure — `_runSkillCommand` measures CRAP 15.45 > 12.0**

The `CRAP + duplication` CI job failed on head `310a70a8` at the **CRAP ratchet** step (job log, step 11 — the only failing step; all duplication/jscpd/dupx/loc gates pass):

```
15.45   75.6  N/A   13  AgentCliSkillsExt._runSkillCommand   lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:338
CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```

This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve decision block added ~4 branches). At the merged-shard coverage of 75.6%, CRAP = 13²·(1−0.756)³ + 13 = **15.45**, over the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold (`crap4dart.yaml`). The rework head's green `ci_failures.md` report was stale relative to this failure.

Fix along the repo's established split-by-concern pattern (AGENTS.md: split by concern, never by extracting public API): pull the whole "skill == null" resolution block into a private helper, e.g.

```dart
/// gh-1440: resolves a `/skill:` name that missed the enabled index —
/// toggled-off report, cold-resolve via full re-discovery, or the exact
/// `unknown skill` wording. Returns the skill when resolved.
Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }
```

Then `_runSkillCommand` becomes:

```dart
var skill = _enabledSkills.where(...).firstOrNull;
skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);
if (skill == null) return; // helper already printed why
```

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'
    ' — enable with /skills on ${skill.name}',
  );
}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers

        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:

print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"

fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;

esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

At the merged-shard coverage of 75.6%, CRAP = 13²·(1−0.756)³ + 13 = **15.45**, over the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold (`crap4dart.yaml`). The rework head's green `ci_failures.md` report was stale relative to this failure.

Fix along the repo's established split-by-concern pattern (AGENTS.md: split by concern, never by extracting public API): pull the whole "skill == null" resolution block into a private helper, e.g.

```dart
/// gh-1440: resolves a `/skill:` name that missed the enabled index —
/// toggled-off report, cold-resolve via full re-discovery, or the exact
/// `unknown skill` wording. Returns the skill when resolved.
Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }
```

Then `_runSkillCommand` becomes:

```dart
var skill = _enabledSkills.where(...).firstOrNull;
skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);
if (skill == null) return; // helper already printed why
```

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'
    ' — enable with /skills on ${skill.name}',
  );
}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown

---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then

fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;

  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;

AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"

# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish

  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in

  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;

  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;

  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac

  CUR="{}"

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

### Root cause of the red CI (fetched the real job log — the rework summary was stale)
The `CRAP + duplication` job failed on head `310a70a8` at **step 11, "CRAP ratchet"**:
```

CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```
This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve block added ~4 branches); at 75.6% merged coverage that measures CRAP 15.45 against the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold. I verified locally that every *other* gate in that job passes (`check --baseline`, loc-scope gate, jscpd 0.82% < 1%, dupx 0.23% < 0.31%), and the new test suites (21 + 51 tests) all pass — so the CRAP ratchet is the sole blocker.

### Findings
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** (`skill_commands.dart:340`) — CRAP ratchet failure; extract the miss-resolution (disabled report + cold-resolve + `unknown skill`) into a `Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss()` helper per the repo's split-by-concern pattern → CC ~9, CRAP ≈ 10.2, back under threshold.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`skill_commands.dart:367`) — the disabled-skill message is duplicated with inconsistent wording: `skill off is disabled (project)` (indexed) vs `skill off is (project) disabled` (cold-resolve). One shared helper fixes the inconsistency and feeds the CRAP fix.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`skill_commands.dart:151`) — the new fingerprint is latched *before* `_reloadSkills()`; a mid-rescan failure keeps the old index but the fresh baseline, so the rescan is never retried (weakens I2).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`frontmatter_parser.dart:73`) — empty/comment-only frontmatter (`---\n---`) loads to `null`, fails `is Map`, and is now skipped as "malformed" where it previously loaded with defaults; consider accepting `null` as well-formed-empty.

### What checked out clean
Architecture (pure fingerprint module, `_reloadSkills` reuse, consent-filtered roots per I3), security posture (provenance `added mid-session` flag rendered, full-discovery cold-resolve per I4, no new grant/execution surface), barrel append-only policy, AC coverage (UT/IT/E2E all present and passing), and the spilling-test normalizer fix.

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit

    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241

) || true

SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"

fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish

gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \

  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"
  ARGS=(api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}"
    -f branch="${DATA_BRANCH}"
    -f message="leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]"
    -f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)")

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### Root cause of the red CI (fetched the real job log — the rework summary was stale)
The `CRAP + duplication` job failed on head `310a70a8` at **step 11, "CRAP ratchet"**:
```

CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```
This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve block added ~4 branches); at 75.6% merged coverage that measures CRAP 15.45 against the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold. I verified locally that every *other* gate in that job passes (`check --baseline`, loc-scope gate, jscpd 0.82% < 1%, dupx 0.23% < 0.31%), and the new test suites (21 + 51 tests) all pass — so the CRAP ratchet is the sole blocker.

### Findings
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** (`skill_commands.dart:340`) — CRAP ratchet failure; extract the miss-resolution (disabled report + cold-resolve + `unknown skill`) into a `Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss()` helper per the repo's split-by-concern pattern → CC ~9, CRAP ≈ 10.2, back under threshold.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`skill_commands.dart:367`) — the disabled-skill message is duplicated with inconsistent wording: `skill off is disabled (project)` (indexed) vs `skill off is (project) disabled` (cold-resolve). One shared helper fixes the inconsistency and feeds the CRAP fix.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`skill_commands.dart:151`) — the new fingerprint is latched *before* `_reloadSkills()`; a mid-rescan failure keeps the old index but the fresh baseline, so the rescan is never retried (weakens I2).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`frontmatter_parser.dart:73`) — empty/comment-only frontmatter (`---\n---`) loads to `null`, fails `is Map`, and is now skipped as "malformed" where it previously loaded with defaults; consider accepting `null` as well-formed-empty.

### What checked out clean
Architecture (pure fingerprint module, `_reloadSkills` reuse, consent-filtered roots per I3), security posture (provenance `added mid-session` flag rendered, full-discovery cold-resolve per I4, no new grant/execution surface), barrel append-only policy, AC coverage (UT/IT/E2E all present and passing), and the spilling-test normalizer fix.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;

}
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### Root cause of the red CI (fetched the real job log — the rework summary was stale)
The `CRAP + duplication` job failed on head `310a70a8` at **step 11, "CRAP ratchet"**:
```
15.45   75.6  N/A   13  AgentCliSkillsExt._runSkillCommand   lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:338
CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```
This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve block added ~4 branches); at 75.6% merged coverage that measures CRAP 15.45 against the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold. I verified locally that every *other* gate in that job passes (`check --baseline`, loc-scope gate, jscpd 0.82% < 1%, dupx 0.23% < 0.31%), and the new test suites (21 + 51 tests) all pass — so the CRAP ratchet is the sole blocker.

### Findings
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** (`skill_commands.dart:340`) — CRAP ratchet failure; extract the miss-resolution (disabled report + cold-resolve + `unknown skill`) into a `Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss()` helper per the repo's split-by-concern pattern → CC ~9, CRAP ≈ 10.2, back under threshold.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`skill_commands.dart:367`) — the disabled-skill message is duplicated with inconsistent wording: `skill off is disabled (project)` (indexed) vs `skill off is (project) disabled` (cold-resolve). One shared helper fixes the inconsistency and feeds the CRAP fix.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`skill_commands.dart:151`) — the new fingerprint is latched *before* `_reloadSkills()`; a mid-rescan failure keeps the old index but the fresh baseline, so the rescan is never retried (weakens I2).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`frontmatter_parser.dart:73`) — empty/comment-only frontmatter (`---\n---`) loads to `null`, fails `is Map`, and is now skipped as "malformed" where it previously loaded with defaults; consider accepting `null` as well-formed-empty.

### What checked out clean
Architecture (pure fingerprint module, `_reloadSkills` reuse, consent-filtered roots per I3), security posture (provenance `added mid-session` flag rendered, full-discovery cold-resolve per I4, no new grant/execution surface), barrel append-only policy, AC coverage (UT/IT/E2E all present and passing), and the spilling-test normalizer fix.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit

    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241

blocks.text:
Review complete. All artifacts are written to `outputs/`.

## Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES

### Root cause of the red CI (fetched the real job log — the rework summary was stale)
The `CRAP + duplication` job failed on head `310a70a8` at **step 11, "CRAP ratchet"**:
```
15.45   75.6  N/A   13  AgentCliSkillsExt._runSkillCommand   lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:338
CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```
This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve block added ~4 branches); at 75.6% merged coverage that measures CRAP 15.45 against the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold. I verified locally that every *other* gate in that job passes (`check --baseline`, loc-scope gate, jscpd 0.82% < 1%, dupx 0.23% < 0.31%), and the new test suites (21 + 51 tests) all pass — so the CRAP ratchet is the sole blocker.

### Findings
- 🚨 **BLOCKING** (`skill_commands.dart:340`) — CRAP ratchet failure; extract the miss-resolution (disabled report + cold-resolve + `unknown skill`) into a `Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss()` helper per the repo's split-by-concern pattern → CC ~9, CRAP ≈ 10.2, back under threshold.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** (`skill_commands.dart:367`) — the disabled-skill message is duplicated with inconsistent wording: `skill off is disabled (project)` (indexed) vs `skill off is (project) disabled` (cold-resolve). One shared helper fixes the inconsistency and feeds the CRAP fix.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`skill_commands.dart:151`) — the new fingerprint is latched *before* `_reloadSkills()`; a mid-rescan failure keeps the old index but the fresh baseline, so the rescan is never retried (weakens I2).
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** (`frontmatter_parser.dart:73`) — empty/comment-only frontmatter (`---\n---`) loads to `null`, fails `is Map`, and is now skipped as "malformed" where it previously loaded with defaults; consider accepting `null` as well-formed-empty.

### What checked out clean
Architecture (pure fingerprint module, `_reloadSkills` reuse, consent-filtered roots per I3), security posture (provenance `added mid-session` flag rendered, full-discovery cold-resolve per I4, no new grant/execution surface), barrel append-only policy, AC coverage (UT/IT/E2E all present and passing), and the spilling-test normalizer fix.

Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
