import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers

        if rec.get("model"):

print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

> ℹ️ **4 resolved thread(s) excluded; 12 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The design is sound — fingerprint-gated rescan reusing `_reloadSkills`, full-discovery cold-resolve, consent-filtered roots (I3), prompt disclosure with the `added mid-session` provenance flag — and the UT/IT/E2E coverage is thorough (all ACs exercised; REG suites verified green locally). However the `CRAP + duplication` CI job fails on the current head `310a70a8`: the CRAP ratchet step reports `_runSkillCommand` at **15.45 > 12.0** (CC grew 9→13 in this PR, 75.6% coverage), which blocks merge by the repo's own ratchet rule. The rework summary's claim that only the (fixed) spilling test was red is stale — I reproduced the failure from the live job log; all other gates in that job (Type-2 duplication baseline, jscpd <1%, dupx, loc) pass locally.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 CRAP ratchet failure in `_runSkillCommand` (extract the cold-resolve resolution block into a private helper — the repo's standard split-by-concern pattern)
- ⚠️ Disabled-skill message duplicated with inconsistent wording between the indexed and cold-resolve paths
- 💡 Failing rescan latches the new fingerprint while keeping the old index (no retry); empty/comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed

**Next Steps**:
1. Extract the `/skill:` miss-resolution (disabled report + cold-resolve + `unknown skill`) into a `Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name)` helper — brings CC back under the CRAP threshold
2. Fold both disabled-skill messages into one shared helper (fixes the wording inconsistency)
3. Re-run the `CRAP + duplication` job to green

---

### Thread 10

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CRAP ratchet failure — `_runSkillCommand` measures CRAP 15.45 > 12.0**

The `CRAP + duplication` CI job failed on head `310a70a8` at the **CRAP ratchet** step (job log, step 11 — the only failing step; all duplication/jscpd/dupx/loc gates pass):

```
15.45   75.6  N/A   13  AgentCliSkillsExt._runSkillCommand   lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:338
CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```

This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve decision block added ~4 branches). At the merged-shard coverage of 75.6%, CRAP = 13²·(1−0.756)³ + 13 = **15.45**, over the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold (`crap4dart.yaml`). The rework head's green `ci_failures.md` report was stale relative to this failure.

Fix along the repo's established split-by-concern pattern (AGENTS.md: split by concern, never by extracting public API): pull the whole "skill == null" resolution block into a private helper, e.g.

```dart
/// gh-1440: resolves a `/skill:` name that missed the enabled index —
/// toggled-off report, cold-resolve via full re-discovery, or the exact
/// `unknown skill` wording. Returns the skill when resolved.
Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }
```

Then `_runSkillCommand` becomes:

```dart
var skill = _enabledSkills.where(...).firstOrNull;
skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);
if (skill == null) return; // helper already printed why
```

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'
    ' — enable with /skills on ${skill.name}',
  );
}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish

gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"
  ARGS=(api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}"
    -f branch="${DATA_BRANCH}"
    -f message="leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]"
    -f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)")

boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```

1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"
  ARGS=(api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}"
    -f branch="${DATA_BRANCH}"
    -f message="leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]"
    -f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)")

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1461 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1461 - **Title**: gh-1440 [GOAL] Skills discovery freshness — a mid-session-added skill must not be invisible (index is a cache, not truth) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1440` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 19 - **Additions**: +1615 - **Deletions**: -43 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T21:14:13Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-10T01:57:34Z ## PR Description Closes #1440 ### What changed Skills discovery is now fresh, not boot-frozen: a stat-level fingerprint of the skill roots (one `listDir` per root, metadata only) gates a rescan at every prompt composition, so a `SKILL.md` dropped mid-session joins the index without a restart, and `/skill:` of an on-disk-but-unindexed skill cold-resolves through full discovery instead of answering `unknown skill`. ### Key decisions - New `skills_freshness.dart`: pure fingerprint (`name:kind:size:mtimeMs` per entry, sorted), no `dart:io` — hosts get the check for free via `ExecutionEnv` - Rescans ride the existing `_reloadSkills` (same roots, consent gate, toggles) — no second discovery path; boot now uses it too - `formatSkillsForPrompt` renders `scanned at ` only from the LAST SCAN's wall-clock, so an unchanged fingerprint renders a byte-identical section (no session-JSONL churn); mid-session arrivals carry an `added mid-session ()` flag, also shown by `/skills` - Malformed frontmatter (torn write) is skipped with a warn-once note via the new `frontmatterWellFormed` check instead of indexing a half-entry; discovery stays tolerant for all other callers - Freshness-check IO failures degrade to one dim warning + last good index; a dropped skill prints a one-line note on the next scan; `skills.liveRediscovery: false` (config, strict-parsed, default on) restores boot-snapshot semantics with a visible staleness footer — `/skills reload` and cold-resolve stay available either way - Auto-continues never rescan mid-turn (bounded cost: one listing per root per turn, zero body reads) ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/skills/skills_freshness_test.dart test/cli/skills_freshness_cli_test.dart dart test test/integration/skills_freshness_pty_test.dart --tags pty ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD TURN[user prompt / composition] --> FP[compute fingerprint
1 listDir per root] FP -->|unchanged| KEEP[byte-identical prompt section] FP -->|changed| RELOAD[_reloadSkills — full discovery] INV[/skill:name miss/] --> COLD[cold-resolve via discovery] RELOAD --> FLAG[added mid-session flag + scan stamp] COLD --> FLAG ```

/// gh-1440: resolves a `/skill:` name that missed the enabled index —

Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }

Then `_runSkillCommand` becomes:

```dart
var skill = _enabledSkills.where(...).firstOrNull;
skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);
if (skill == null) return; // helper already printed why
```

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'
    ' — enable with /skills on ${skill.name}',
  );
}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then

case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in

  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;

  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;

  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac

  CUR="{}"

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The design is sound — fingerprint-gated rescan reusing `_reloadSkills`, full-discovery cold-resolve, consent-filtered roots (I3), prompt disclosure with the `added mid-session` provenance flag — and the UT/IT/E2E coverage is thorough (all ACs exercised; REG suites verified green locally). However the `CRAP + duplication` CI job fails on the current head `310a70a8`: the CRAP ratchet step reports `_runSkillCommand` at **15.45 > 12.0** (CC grew 9→13 in this PR, 75.6% coverage), which blocks merge by the repo's own ratchet rule. The rework summary's claim that only the (fixed) spilling test was red is stale — I reproduced the failure from the live job log; all other gates in that job (Type-2 duplication baseline, jscpd <1%, dupx, loc) pass locally.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 CRAP ratchet failure in `_runSkillCommand` (extract the cold-resolve resolution block into a private helper — the repo's standard split-by-concern pattern)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

🚨 **BLOCKING: CRAP ratchet failure — `_runSkillCommand` measures CRAP 15.45 > 12.0**

The `CRAP + duplication` CI job failed on head `310a70a8` at the **CRAP ratchet** step (job log, step 11 — the only failing step; all duplication/jscpd/dupx/loc gates pass):

```
15.45   75.6  N/A   13  AgentCliSkillsExt._runSkillCommand   lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart:338
CRAP threshold exceeded: 15.45 > 12.0
```

This PR grew `_runSkillCommand` from CC ~9 to **CC 13** (the cold-resolve decision block added ~4 branches). At the merged-shard coverage of 75.6%, CRAP = 13²·(1−0.756)³ + 13 = **15.45**, over the repo-pinned 12.0 threshold (`crap4dart.yaml`). The rework head's green `ci_failures.md` report was stale relative to this failure.

Fix along the repo's established split-by-concern pattern (AGENTS.md: split by concern, never by extracting public API): pull the whole "skill == null" resolution block into a private helper, e.g.

```dart
/// gh-1440: resolves a `/skill:` name that missed the enabled index —
/// toggled-off report, cold-resolve via full re-discovery, or the exact
/// `unknown skill` wording. Returns the skill when resolved.
Future<Skill?> _resolveSkillMiss(String name) async { ... }
```

Then `_runSkillCommand` becomes:

```dart
var skill = _enabledSkills.where(...).firstOrNull;
skill ??= await _resolveSkillMiss(name);
if (skill == null) return; // helper already printed why
```

That removes ~4 branches (CC → ~9 ⇒ CRAP ≈ 10.2 at the same coverage, back under the threshold), and the helper is also the natural home for the disabled-skill message shared with the indexed path (see the adjacent IMPORTANT comment).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: duplicated disabled-skill message with inconsistent wording**

The disabled-skill report is now written twice with **different word order**:

- Indexed path (line ~346): `'skill ${disabled.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'` → renders `skill off is disabled (project)`
- Cold-resolve path (here, line ~367): `'skill ${coldDisabled.name} is' '${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'} disabled'` → renders `skill off is (project) disabled`

The two paths answer the same state with grammatically different output, and the copy-paste also feeds the `_runSkillCommand` complexity that tripped the CRAP gate. Extract one shared helper, e.g.

```dart
void _reportDisabledSkill(Skill skill) {
  final scope = _skillResolution.byName[skill.name]?.scope?.name;
  io.writeln(
    'skill ${skill.name} is disabled${scope == null ? '' : ' ($scope)'}'
    ' — enable with /skills on ${skill.name}',
  );
}
```

and call it from both branches (the indexed branch and `_resolveSkillMiss`'s `coldDisabled` branch). The existing IT-4 assertions (`skill off is disabled`, `/skills on off`) keep passing unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a failing rescan latches the new fingerprint but keeps the old index — the rescan is never retried**

The pre-assignment (documented as the I5 re-entrancy guard) updates `_skillRootsFingerprint` to the *new* value before `_reloadSkills()` runs. If the rescan itself throws (e.g. `_resolveSkillAvailability`/`_applyPromptComposition` fails — the `on Object catch` below handles exactly that), the catch keeps the old `_skills` index, but the baseline now matches the new tree: every later turn sees `fingerprint == baseline` and the rescan never retries until the disk changes again. That weakens I2 ("keeps the last good snapshot" — but the check is now blind to the stale index).

Safer shape: assign the new fingerprint only after the rescan succeeds (the `_noteSkillScan` recompute already overwrites it on success, so the pre-assignment only has an effect in the failure window):

```dart
if (baseline == null || fingerprint == baseline) return;
await _reloadSkills(); // _noteSkillScan records the fresh fingerprint
```

If the re-entrant-check concern is real, a `_rescanning` bool latch gives the same at-most-one-rescan guarantee without coupling the failure path.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

💡 **SUGGESTION: empty or comment-only frontmatter now counts as malformed and gets skipped**

`loadYaml` returns `null` for an empty yaml block (and for a comment-only block), so a `SKILL.md` whose frontmatter is

```markdown
---
---
body
```

or `---\n# note\n---` fails the `is Map` check here and is now skipped with a "malformed frontmatter" warning — whereas before this change it loaded fine (fallback name from the directory, empty description). The warning makes the degradation loud rather than silent, so this is not blocking, but an empty fence is arguably well-formed "no metadata" rather than a torn write (E-1). Consider accepting `null`:

```dart
final yaml = loadYaml(text.substring(3, end));
return yaml == null || yaml is Map;
```

If the strict reading is intentional (every indexed skill must carry a parsed map), a one-line doc note on `frontmatterWellFormed` would settle it.

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish
# (422 "already exists" is the normal case) — then PUT with the
# existing sha; 3 attempts absorb concurrent leg publishes.
gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"

read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers

        if rec.get("model"):

print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true

Can the PR fix it? The failure mechanism depends on the fa-tokens line lacking `"model"`. Interesting angle: the factory script reads `rec.get("model")` from the fa-tokens JSON. The fa ledger line is produced by THIS repo's code (`usage_log_line.dart`). gh-1241's comment says "the fa ledger carries it once gh-1241 grows the field; absent today — stay empty". So the factory kit was updated in anticipation, and the fa side hasn't grown the field yet — and the kit's shell has an extraction bug for the absent case. The clean fix is factory-side (read 3 vars properly) OR fa-side (add the model field to the ledger — but the shape is AC7-pinned by a regex test, so adding a field would require updating the pinned pattern + reporter... which IS in this repo's power!).

Hmm wait — could this PR add `"model"` to the fa-tokens line? So: the red check is unfixable within this PR's scope. What does the review protocol demand? "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)". And verdict rules: any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES.

Option A: REQUEST_CHANGES with the factory failure as BLOCKING → rework leg re-arms → rework agent finds nothing to fix (or worse, "fixes" something irrelevant) → factory fails again → loop forever, burning CI.

Option B: APPROVE with the factory failure reported as an IMPORTANT/non-blocking finding + prose explaining it's factory infra, needs owner/factory-kit fix. The machine merges? One PR-fixable angle: the rework agent's run output also could include a "model" field if the agent printed it — no, the ledger line is printed by fa itself, not the agent.

So truly not PR-fixable. 

Given the explicit instruction hierarchy — the formatting rule F7 is unconditional ("include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING") — I'll include it as BLOCKING in the report, but the recommendation must weigh the machine-loop anti-pattern. The verdict rules' stated intent: "each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71" and anti-patterns warn against non-converging cycles. A REQUEST_CHANGES here guarantees a wasted round (nothing in the PR can fix a factory-kit shell bug). import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"

# Sum every fa-tokens ledger line (resume-aware: one line per
# session segment). Balanced-brace JSON after the marker.
read -r SUM_IN SUM_OUT < <(python3 - "${RUN_OUTPUT}" <<'PY' || true
import json, re, sys
inp = out = 0
model = ""
try:
    text = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
except OSError:
    print(0, 0, ""); raise SystemExit
for m in re.finditer(r"fa-tokens:[ \t]*(\{)", text):
    depth, i = 0, m.start(1)
    for i in range(m.start(1), len(text)):
        if text[i] == "{": depth += 1
        elif text[i] == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: break
    try:
        rec = json.loads(text[m.start(1):i + 1])
        inp += int(rec.get("input") or 0)
        out += int(rec.get("output") or 0)
        # last-seen model wins (fa ledger carries it once gh-1241
        # grows the field; absent today — stay empty, consumers
        # render tokens-only)
        if rec.get("model"):
            model = str(rec["model"])
    except Exception:
        continue
print(inp, out, model)
PY
) || true
SUM_IN="${SUM_IN:-0}"
SUM_OUT="${SUM_OUT:-0}"
MODEL="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $3}')"
SUM_OUT="$(echo "${SUM_OUT}" | awk '{print $2}')"
if [ "${SUM_IN}" = "0" ] && [ "${SUM_OUT}" = "0" ]; then
  echo "::warning::no fa-tokens ledger line in run output — skipping token publish"
  exit 0
fi
# The guard collapses the rework slot into kind="dev" (rework legs run the
# dev pipeline); recover the true leg from the runner config basename.
case "$(basename "${CONFIG:-}" .json)" in
  *rework*) LEG="rework" ;;
  *) LEG="${KIND:-dev}" ;;
esac
case "${ANCHOR}" in
  pr-*) KEY="${ANCHOR}" ;;
  gh-*) KEY="issue-${ANCHOR#gh-}" ;;
  *) echo "::warning::unrecognized anchor '${ANCHOR}' — skipping token publish"; exit 0 ;;
esac
AT="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
ROW="$(printf '{"leg":"%s","at":"%s","prompt":%s,"completion":%s,"total":%s,"model":"%s"}' \
  "${LEG}" "${AT}" "${SUM_IN}" "${SUM_OUT}" "$((SUM_IN + SUM_OUT))" "${MODEL}")"
echo "leg tokens: ${KEY} ${LEG} prompt=${SUM_IN} completion=${SUM_OUT} model=${MODEL:-none}"
# Bootstrap the data branch exactly like the tick's state publish

gh api "repos/${REPO}/git/ref/heads/$(gh api "repos/${REPO}" --jq .default_branch)" \
  --jq .object.sha \
  | xargs -I{} gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/git/refs" -f ref="refs/heads/${DATA_BRANCH}" -f sha={} || true
ok=0
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  SHA=""
  CUR="{}"
  if META="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}?ref=${DATA_BRANCH}" 2>/dev/null)"; then
    SHA="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .sha)"
    CUR="$(printf %s "${META}" | jq -r .content | tr -d '\n' | base64 -d 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"
    printf %s "${CUR}" | jq empty >/dev/null 2>&1 || CUR='{}'
  fi
  CUTOFF="$(python3 -c "import datetime; print((datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc) - datetime.timedelta(days=14)).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))")"
  NEXT="$(printf %s "${CUR}" | jq --argjson row "${ROW}" --arg key "${KEY}" --arg cutoff "${CUTOFF}" \
    '.[$key] = ((.[$key] // []) + [$row])
     | with_entries(.value |= (map(select((.at // "") >= $cutoff)) | .[-40:]))
     | with_entries(select(.value | length > 0))')"
  ARGS=(api -X PUT "repos/${REPO}/contents/${DATA_PATH}"
    -f branch="${DATA_BRANCH}"
    -f message="leg tokens — ${KEY} ${LEG} [skip ci]"
    -f content="$(printf %s "${NEXT}" | base64)")
